text:
Mei: Noticing a pattern on the per-model mini-card: cache savings frequently exceed token_cost in low-volume routes. Example: tenant L, route /api/parse -> cost $0.05, cache_savings $0.17. Screenshot in thread.
Jorge: Thanks Mei. Is this the 24h panel or billing view?
Mei: 24h exploration. I grabbed the rollup row: token_cost_24h=0.05, cache_credit_24h=0.17, sample_coverage=8%.
Anika: low coverage explains a lot. If the cache-crediting pipeline sampled a span that's not represented in token rows we can attribute full amortization to a tiny token bucket.
Theo: short-term UI fix idea: show "Estimated cache savings" and clamp it client-side to min(cache_credit_24h, token_cost_24h) when sample_coverage < 25%. Add a confidence pill (low/med/high).
Jorge: I like that. But we must not silently change what billing consumers see. Backend should expose canonical fields: cache_credit_24h, cache_credit_7d_amortized, token_cost_24h, sample_coverage. Console composes the clamped view.
Anika: Agree. Backend task: emit both windows + sample_count/provenance (RED-ENG-7200). Console task: compute clamped_display_savings behind flag + confidence pill (RED-ENG-7201).
Mei: UX microcopy proposal: "Estimated cache savings (clamped). Based on sampled telemetry; see confidence and amortization basis"
Theo: Also propose an anomaly rule: if cache_credit_24h > token_cost_24h * 2 AND sample_coverage < 30% -> create QA ticket (non-billing). That'll catch weird spikes.
Jorge: I'll add the alert (RED-ENG-7202). For the longer-term fix we should propagate sampled_span_id from router -> cache-cred pipeline so rollup joins are deterministic (RED-ENG-7203).
Anika: timeline: backend schema change this week, console flag next week, canary 10 tenants for 48h.
telemetry-bot: Created issues RED-ENG-7200, RED-ENG-7201, RED-ENG-7202, RED-ENG-7203 and scheduled RED-ENG-7201 canary (env=canary).
Mei: I'll attach sample logs and the tenant row to RED-ENG-7200. Also adding a couple of test vectors: token_count=0 + cache_hits>0 and low-coverage spans.
Jorge: Thanks. After canary we'll decide if clamped view becomes default. We should include a toggle so power users can see raw numbers with provenance.
Anika: Good point. Toggle default: exploration -> clamped; billing -> canonical 7d amortized. Document the differences in the tooltip.
Theo: Ok I'll wire the confidence pill states: low (<25%), med (25-75%), high (>75%). Use faded color for low.
Mei: Great. Meeting to sync on rollout Friday 9:30. Thanks all :thumbsup:
